official.international_eligibility: Yes - the scheme is designed for students who have graduated from a foreign university and is therefore open to applicants of any nationality, provided the foreign degree is recognised as equivalent to a Swiss bachelor's degree.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: It is not possible to apply for the following master programmes: Master from the School of Medicine; Master in Sciences and Practices of Education; Master of Law, with the exception of the specialisms 'International and Comparative Law', 'Legal Theory' and 'International Tax Law and Policy'; Master of Science in Physical Education and Sport Didactics; Master of Science in Health Sciences; Master of Science in Sustainable Management & Technology; Master of Science in Human Taphonomy; and all MASs. Candidates who want to apply for a Master in Finance, Psychology, Arts, or Nursing must fulfil additional conditions published on the Admissions Service (SII) page. The admission conditions for some master programmes can change for the academic year 2027/2028.
official.duration: The minimum statutory period of the chosen Master's programme
official.description: Unil awards around ten excellence scholarships each year, exclusively to students who have graduated from a foreign university and whose academic results are of a very high standard. The scholarship is awarded for the minimum statutory period of the Master's programme and amounts to CHF 1,600 per month; Unil states that because this amount does not cover the full cost of living in Switzerland, the scholarship does not constitute full funding.
official.program_type: University excellence scholarship for international master's admission
official.english_requirement: A minimum C1 level (CEFR) in the language in which the chosen master is taught. For a master taught in English: TOEFL CBT 250, TOEFL IBT 100, TOEFL PBT 600, Academic IELTS 7, Cambridge English Advanced (CAE) Grade B, Cambridge English Proficiency (CPE) Grade C, or TOEIC 850; the diploma should not be older than 2 years. For a master taught in French: DALF level C1 or C2, TCF Tout public level C1 or higher obtained with the 5 components, Certificat de qualification en français (CQF) of Le Fil de l'EFLE level C1 to the four exams, or European Language Certificate (TELC) level C1. No language certificate is required if the master programme chosen at Unil is taught in the mother tongue of the candidate or the bachelor's studies were entirely taught in that language.

applicant_utility.summary: File one single PDF through the UNIL Mastergrants portal and understand that the same file doubles as your admission application - there is no separate Admissions Office route, so this competition effectively decides both the money and your place. Budget for roughly CHF 2,000 a month to live in Lausanne against a CHF 1,600 monthly stipend, because UNIL only waives the course registration fees and leaves rent, health insurance and daily living costs to you. Screen your programme against the excluded list before you invest any effort: Medicine, Sciences and Practices of Education, most of Law, Health Sciences, Sustainable Management & Technology and all MAS programmes are closed, while Finance, Psychology, Arts and Nursing carry extra admission conditions.
applicant_utility.best_fit: A recent graduate of a foreign university with a very strong transcript who wants a UNIL master's in an eligible faculty and can top up the stipend by about CHF 400 per month from family, savings or student work.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your chosen master is not on the excluded list, and check the additional conditions page if you are aiming at Finance, Psychology, Arts or Nursing.
Start the CHF 200 bank transfer early and quote 'Master's Scholarship - your first and last name' exactly; the fee is non-refundable even if you withdraw or are refused.
Brief your two referees to write from institutional (not Gmail/Hotmail) addresses and to put your full name in the e-mail, and remind them the letters only count if sent after you register online.
Check whether your country has ratified the Lisbon Recognition Convention; if not, get sealed certified copies posted in time to carry a 1 November postmark.

Sit your IELTS 7 or TOEFL IBT 100 with enough margin that the certificate is under two years old at the deadline, or verify that your bachelor was taught entirely in the programme language to be exempt.
Assemble the PDF in the exact listed order and re-read the page for updates, since admission conditions for some programmes may change for 2027/2028.
common_rejection_risks: An incomplete PDF, a missing recommendation letter, or missing certified copies where they are required - UNIL states plainly that such files are not taken into account.
Applying to an excluded programme, or to a Law specialism that is not one of the three named exceptions.
Recommendation letters sent from a private e-mail address, or sent before the online registration was submitted.
Having already begun a master's programme at Unil, or being in the UNIL preparatory year.

Being refused a visa because of age or an existing master's degree if you come from a visa-restricted country - UNIL explicitly advises checking with the Swiss diplomatic representation before applying.
Arriving without supplementary funds and being unable to sustain roughly CHF 400 per month beyond the stipend.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Roughly CHF 400 per month of living costs on top of the stipend, plus the CHF 80 semester fees, FMEL rent (student-paid but cheaper than the private market), health insurance, books and materials, and all travel to and from Lausanne - UNIL publishes no travel figure.
document_audit: The PDF must contain every item in the exact published order; an out-of-order or single missing page is treated as an incomplete file.
Authenticated translations are needed for diplomas and transcripts outside French, German, English and Italian - including the high school diploma, which applicants most often forget.

If your degree is not yet awarded you must supply all existing grade transcripts plus a precise description of the remaining programme: courses to follow, credits to obtain, and the dissertation topic.
If you have graduated but not yet received the diploma, supply an official certificate of success with 'degree obtained, graduated' signed by the awarding institution.

Hague Apostille and certifications by secondary schools, the police, town halls or notaries are explicitly not accepted for certified true copies - only the issuing university may certify, in a sealed envelope with a covering letter giving the certifying officer's full contact details.
alerts: A single deadline of 1 November covers three separate submissions - the online PDF, the two reference e-mails and the postmark date for certified copies - so a late letter is fatal even with a perfect PDF.
The Selection Board decides in March and applicants are notified in early April, only weeks before enrolment, so keep other applications alive until then.
Withdrawal from the master programme leads to suspension of the scholarship.
If your scholarship application fails but the faculty admits you, you can still register through the Admissions Office for the same academic year without paying the CHF 200 fee a second time.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register online and upload one ordered PDF by 1 November; referees e-mail their letters to mastergrants@unil.ch after that; certified copies go by post if your country has not ratified the Lisbon Convention; SASME checks completeness, the SII rules on formal eligibility, the faculty rules on admission, and the Selection Board for the Master's Scholarship decides in March.

official.application_route: Online application to a published Doctoral Student Programme vacancy on the CERN careers portal with a CV in English or French; applications are reviewed, shortlisted candidates are interviewed online, and successful candidates receive an offer.
official.citizenship_residency: You must be a national of a CERN Member State or Associate Member State. Applications from Pakistani, Lithuanian, Latvian, Cypriot, Croatian and Turkish nationals currently cannot be considered because the ceiling defined under Article II.5 of the Associate Membership Agreement has been reached. CERN's Member States are Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Israel, Italy, Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Serbia, Slovak Republic, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland and the United Kingdom; its Associate Member States are Brazil, Chile, Croatia, Cyprus, India, Ireland, Latvia, Lithuania, Pakistan, Türkiye and Ukraine.
official.international_eligibility: Restricted to nationals of CERN Member States and Associate Member States. Nationals of other countries are not eligible for this programme, even if their thesis research would be carried out at CERN.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Your university must accept that the research you conduct at CERN contributes to your doctoral thesis in one of CERN's fields of work, and your field of study should align with CERN's research areas including, but not limited to, physics, engineering, computing and related applied sciences. The current round is advertised under Applied Physics, Chemical Materials & Process Engineering, Data Science AI & Analytics, Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Information Technologies and Mechanical Engineering.
official.research_requirement: Your university must support your participation by agreeing that the research you conduct at CERN will contribute to your PhD thesis, and the field of study must align with CERN's research areas. No written research proposal is required at the application stage.
official.duration: 12 to 36 month contract for the 2027-1 round; the programme overall runs on a 6-month contract renewable up to 3 years, with the possibility of spreading it over a maximum duration of 4 consecutive years to allow you to spend time at your university
official.description: The CERN Doctoral Student Programme is a PhD-level employment contract in Geneva in which doctoral students carry out cutting-edge research at CERN in collaboration with their home university, in fields such as applied physics, computing, engineering and related technical areas. It pays a monthly net allowance of CHF 3,907, coverage by CERN's comprehensive health insurance scheme, possible family supplement and travel to Geneva on joining, and 30 days of paid leave a year.
official.program_type: Paid doctoral studentship (subsistence-allowance contract) at an international research organisation, run jointly with a university
official.english_requirement: A good knowledge of English or French is required, and the CV must be submitted in English or French. No certificate or minimum score is specified. CERN's working languages are English and French, and language training is offered to help acquire the other language.

applicant_utility.summary: Treat this as a job, not a scholarship: you stay enrolled at your own university and keep paying your own tuition, so secure your supervisor's written agreement that the CERN work counts towards your thesis before you even open the form. Nationality is the hard gate - only CERN Member and Associate Member State nationals qualify, and six nationalities are currently blocked by the Article II.5 ceiling, so re-read the live exclusion list on the vacancy itself rather than trusting any secondary site. The CHF 3,907 is a net subsistence allowance with the CERN health insurance contribution deducted from it, and students are not eligible for an installation indemnity, so bring your own deposit money for the Geneva housing market.
applicant_utility.best_fit: A doctoral candidate from an eligible European Member or Associate Member State in applied physics, computing, electronics, electrical, mechanical or chemical and materials engineering who needs a year or more of hands-on work at CERN inside the PhD.
application_readiness_checklist: Get written confirmation from your doctoral supervisor and university that the CERN research will be recognised in your thesis - without it the application is not admissible.
Confirm your nationality is on the CERN Member or Associate Member State list and is not on the current Article II.5 exclusion list, which is reviewed each round.
Write the CV in English or French and target it at the specific Field of Work you are applying under, since CERN routes applications by field.
Treat the 'optional' academic reference letter and transcript as close to mandatory; in a competitive STEM round they are the only academic evidence in the file beyond the CV.
Submit before 23:59 Geneva time on the deadline day, and create a CERN job alert for the next round in case you miss this one or are not shortlisted.
Line up your certificate and degree documents early so any claim in the CV can be substantiated quickly if you are shortlisted.
common_rejection_risks: Nationality: applications from the six nationalities blocked by the Article II.5 ceiling, or from nationals of non-Member States, are not considered at all regardless of profile.
No university agreement that the research conducted at CERN will contribute to the doctoral thesis.
Applying under the wrong Field of Work, so the hiring team never sees the profile that matches their needs.
A CV that is not in English or French, or that omits the technical detail CERN screens on - solid theoretical foundation plus interest in practical application.
Assuming the allowance covers relocation: students receive travel to Geneva at most, and CERN states it offers no direct relocation assistance.
Underestimating the timing - the contract can be spread over up to four consecutive years, so if your university cannot accommodate that rhythm the placement collapses mid-thesis.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: University tuition and enrolment fees at your own institution, the CHIS health insurance contribution deducted from the allowance, the Geneva housing deposit and rent, installation costs beyond any travel lump sum, visa and permit costs where applicable, and living costs during periods spent back at the university rather than at CERN.
document_audit: The CV must be in English or French; other languages are not accepted for this programme.
The reference letter and transcript are formally optional, so an application without them rests entirely on the CV - prepare both anyway.
The application is filed against a specific vacancy reference such as TSC-2027-1/DOCT published per Field of Work, not a single general programme entry, so double-check you are in the right listing.
Read the small print on benefits: the installation indemnity and removal expenses listed on CERN's pay page apply to staff members and graduates, not to students.
alerts: Recruitment is round-based with each vacancy carrying its own deadline; the 2027-1 round closes 16 October 2026 at 23:59 Geneva time, with an ideal start date of 1 April 2027.
The nationality exclusion list is time-limited and can change between rounds, so verify it again before you apply to the next one.

The contract is 6 months renewable up to 3 years and can be spread over a maximum of 4 consecutive years, so plan the university side of the PhD around CERN's calendar and the two-week annual closure.
Visa processing can take up to three months depending on the consulate handling the request.
Onboarding begins with an official welcome session held at the start of each month, so the effective start can slip later than the advertised ideal date.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply online to the live vacancy reference through the 'Apply now' form on careers.cern, wait for the CERN application review and a possible online interview with the hiring manager(s), then accept the offer and start onboarding with the monthly welcome session.
